history.dynasty: Traditionally founded by Arjuna (Pandava); patronage by Travancore kings; early Chera/9th-10th c. renovations claimed by secondary sources (verify)
history.period: Legendary Mahabharata-era origin; one secondary source claims 8th century AD construction - CONFLICT (verify)
history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams revered by the Alvar saints and among the five ancient Kerala Krishna shrines the Pandavas are said to have built (Arjuna's share). Legend: the idol, originally at Nilakkal, was floated here on a raft of six bamboo pieces (aru-mula), giving the name; Arjuna built it as penance for killing Karna. The 6-ft idol shows Krishna in Vishvarupa holding the discus - the image of the moment he picked up the chakra on the 9th day of Kurukshetra. The Uthrittathi Vallamkali originates from the rescue of the Thiruvona Thoni feast boat by snake boats. The temple stores the Thanka Anki (golden attire of Ayyappan) taken to Sabarimala in Mandala season; its wall murals date to the early 18th century. The CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Pathanamthitta' (the district); actual town is Aranmula, state Kerala. Hours conflict: 4 AM-11 AM (most sources) vs 4 AM-12 noon (poojn.in) - verify.

name: Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple
town_description: Aranmula is a heritage village on the southern bank of the Pamba river in Pathanamthitta district, about 9 km from Chengannur. Embroidered with epic legend, it is famed for the Parthasarathy temple, the annual Vallamkali boat race, and the unique Aranmula Kannadi metal mirror craft, plus nearby Kathakali and Vasthu Vidya centres.

travel.road: Well connected by road with Pathanamthitta, Chengannur and Thiruvalla; regular buses and taxis

visitor_information.best_time: August-September for the Uthrittathi Vallamkali and Onam season; December-January for Khandavana Dahanam; October to February otherwise
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM-11:00 AM and 5:00 PM-8:00 PM (Wikipedia, tourmyindia, bharattemples; Travancore Devaswom Board administered) - CONFLICT (verify): poojn.in reports morning close at 12 noon
